questions.question: What is the frequency (f) of a wave with a period of 0.04 seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The frequency (f) of a wave is the reciprocal of its period (T).
 
• The formula to calculate frequency is f = 1/T.
 
• Given the period T = 0.04 seconds, applying the formula gives f = 1/0.04.
 
• Therefore, the frequency of the wave is f = 25 Hz.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency (f)**:

 
 
• Frequency is the number of complete wave cycles that pass a point per unit of time, typically measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• 1 Hz is equal to one cycle per second.
 
 
 
• **Period (T)**:
 
 
• The period is the time taken for one complete cycle of the wave to pass a given point.
 
• It is usually measured in seconds (s).
 
 
 
• **Relationship between Period and Frequency**:
 
 
• The period is the inverse of the frequency: T = 1/f.
 
• Similarly, frequency is the inverse of the period: f = 1/T.
 
 
 
• **Wave Cycles**:
 
 
• A wave cycle consists of one complete wave oscillation, typically measured from crest to crest or trough to trough.

questions.question: The colour of the clear sky is blue due to the phenomenon of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **__Scattering of light.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The blue color of the sky is due to the scattering of light by the atmospheric particles.**
 
• Light of shorter wavelength scatters more than the light of longer wavelengths and the violet color has a shorter wavelength, but our eyes are more sensitive to blue light. Hence, the color of a clear sky is blue.

 

 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a15693d2f6074875647f9304b7593c68cd6d8f00ba9b65d476d212d8cb3df65f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Light is scattered by molecules of dust, and water vapor in the air.
 
• A clear cloudless sky is blue because molecules in the air scatter blue light from the sun more than they scatter red light.
 
• When we look towards the sun at sunset, we see red and orange colors because the blue light has been scattered out and away from the line of sight.
 
• Dispersion: The white light gets split into constituent "VIBGYOR".
 
• Interference: The change in waveform because of the superimposition of two or more light waves.

 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e52795cea1d319d72193029cb65bc2e5fbbf3f91ef21c5f48095470a708d747.png]

questions.question: White light is composed of how many colours?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the 1660s, English physicist and mathematician** Isaac Newton** began a series of experiments with sunlight and prisms.
 
• He demonstrated that clear **white light was composed of seven visible colors**.
 
• One of the greatest scientific **books **ever written, **Opticks**, details** Newton's findings from his experiments using prisms** to bend light.
 
• He named the **hues that comprise the visible spectrum**: **red**, **orange**, **yellow**, **green**, **blue**, **indigo**, and **violet**, or **ROYGBIV**.
 
• The small range of the electromagnetic spectrum that is visible to the human eye is known as the **visible spectrum**.
 
 
• Typically, the human eye can detect wavelengths from **380 to 700 nanometers.**
 
 
 
• Radio, gamma, and microwave radiation are additional types of **electromagnetic radiation**—energy waves that are invisible to the human eye.
 
• **Cone cells**, which are located in human eyes, are sensitive to wavelengths in the visible range. They **make it possible for us to see every hue in the rainbow.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phenomenon of splitting light into its constituent colors is called **dispersion of light**.
 
• The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as **refraction**.

questions.question: Among the given options, which one causes an echo?

options.text: When sound waves travel through a solid medium
When sound waves travel through a liquid medium
When sound waves travel through a vacuum

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **When sound is reflected**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Echo** is a phenomenon where sound waves are reflected back to the listener, causing a repetition of the original sound.
 
• For an echo to be heard, the reflected sound must reach the listener at least 0.1 seconds after the original sound.
 
• The distance between the sound source and the reflecting surface must be significant for an echo to be perceived.
 
• Common environments where echoes are noticed include large empty halls, mountains, and canyons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sound Reflection**: The bouncing back of sound waves when they hit a surface that does not absorb the sound.
 
• **Absorption**: Some materials absorb sound waves, preventing echoes. Examples include carpets and curtains.
 
• **Reverberation**: Unlike an echo, reverberation is the persistence of sound in a particular space after the original sound is produced.
 
• **Acoustic Design**: Modern architecture often incorporates materials and designs to manage echoes and reverberation in buildings.

questions.question: The splitting of white light into its component colours is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dispersion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dispersion is the phenomenon of visible light into its component colours.
 
• Dispersion of light is caused by the change of speed of light rays of each wavelength by a different amount.
 
• It is a property of light.
 
• **Dispersion of light **occurs **when white light is separated into its different constituent colours.**
 
• When white light is passed through a prism, it splits into seven colours.
 
• The colours are** Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction:**

 
 
• **Refraction is the bending of light **as it passes through a** medium, such as air or water, with a different refractive index.**
 
• The amount of bending depends on the angle of** incidence and the properties of the medium.**
 
• This phenomenon is what causes objects in water to** appear distorted or displaced.**
 
 
 
• **Reflection:**
 
 
• **​Reflection **occurs when light rays bounce off a** surface, changing direction.**
 
• The angle at which the light hits the surface, known as the angle of incidence,** is equal to the angle at which the light is reflected, known as the angle of reflection.**
 
• Reflection is what allows us to** see ourselves in mirrors, and is also responsible for the way light interacts with shiny surfaces.**
 
 
 
• **Scattering:**
 
 
• **​**Scattering is the process by which light is redirected in **many different directions when it encounters particles or irregularities in a medium.**
 
• This can cause light to be diffused, making objects appear less sharp or distinct.
 
• **Scattering **is responsible for the **blue colour of the sky, as well as the way light interacts with clouds, fog, and other atmospheric phenomena.**

questions.question: Apart from the red and green wavelengths of sunlight, which other wavelength of sunlight is absorbed by the water molecules in the ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yellow.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Because **water is so good at absorbing light,** the amount of light that gets through to the ocean declines fast (or is attenuated) as you go deeper.
 
• Various wavelengths of light are absorbed at different rates by the oceans.
 
 
• **Longer wavelengths absorb first**; **red** absorbs in the upper** 10 m**, **orange** around **40 m**, and** yellow **around **100 m**.
 
• **Shorter wavelengths** penetrate deeper into the body, with** blue and green** light reaching the** deepest** levels.
 
 
 
• **Blue light** penetrates deeply and is **scattered by the water molecules**, while all other colours are absorbed. Therefore, **the water appears blue**. **Coastal water**, on the other hand, is frequently** greenish**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wavelength** is the distance between identical points (**adjacent crests**) in the adjacent cycles of a waveform signal propagated in space or along a wire

 

 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/327df6b2fc52a37c1b5fd9306188dd4bf7fa80b7335b8f842495e4c150859c22.png]

questions.question: It is observed that a child's heart rate is 135 times per minute. The beat frequency of heart is ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.25 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **heart rate** refers to the number of times the heart beats per minute.
 
• The **beat frequency** of the heart is the number of beats per second.
 
• To convert the heart rate from beats per minute to beats per second, we divide by **60**.
 
• In this scenario, the child's heart rate is **135 times per minute**.
 
• Dividing 135 by 60 gives us the beat frequency: **135/60 = 2.25 Hz**.
 
• Therefore, the beat frequency of the heart is **2.25 Hz**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **8100 Hz**__

 __
 
• This value is **incorrect** as it does not correspond to the heart rate conversion process.
 
• Such a high frequency is more typical of **sound waves** or other high-frequency phenomena.
 
 
 
• **1.12 Hz**__
 __
 
• This value is **incorrect** because it is not the result of dividing 135 by 60.
 
• A beat frequency of 1.12 Hz would correspond to a heart rate of **67.2 beats per minute**, which is much lower than 135 beats per minute.
 
 
 
• **135 Hz**__
 
 
• This value is **incorrect** because it mistakenly assumes that the heart rate in beats per minute is the same as the beat frequency in Hz.
 
• 135 Hz would imply an extremely high heart rate of **8100 beats per minute**, which is not physiologically possible.
